profile.summary: GPN (Genomic Pretrained Network, also called GPN-SS) is a DNA language model that learns from unaligned genome sequences alone. Given a 512-bp DNA window with some positions masked, it predicts the nucleotide at each masked position. Its main use is to score genetic variants without labels: the score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele. The published model was trained on Arabidopsis thaliana and seven other Brassicales genomes.
profile.summary_source_locator: docs/models/gpn.md introduction; paper Fig. 1 caption; model card title

summary_quotes.text: GPN, also known as GPN-SS, is a single-sequence genomic language model trained on unaligned genomes.
The input is a 512-bp DNA sequence where certain positions have been masked, and the goal is to predict the nucleotides at the masked positions.
The GPN variant effect prediction score is defined as the log-likelihood ratio between the alternate and reference allele.
# GPN trained on *Arabidopsis thaliana* and 7 other Brassicales

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GPN is a convolutional neural network, not a transformer. The masked DNA sequence is one-hot encoded with single nucleotides as tokens, then passed through 25 convolutional blocks. Each block has a dilated convolution and a feed-forward layer, with residual connections and layer normalisation; the embedding dimension stays at 512. Training is masked language modelling: 15% of positions are masked and predicted with a cross-entropy loss. To score a variant, only the variant position is masked, and the score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele. The authors down-weighted repetitive elements in the loss; the card records a repeat weight of 0.1.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The songlab-cal/gpn repository now covers four model families: GPN, GPN-MSA, PhyloGPN and GPN-Star. This page is about single-sequence GPN. Its published checkpoint is songlab/gpn-brassicales, which uses a seven-token DNA tokenizer. The same family also has an animal promoter model (songlab/gpn-animal-promoter) and a sorghum gene-expression model fine-tuned from gpn-brassicales. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; this page read gpn-brassicales at revision eb9c35d0. The paper analyses are kept in an archive branch, and the maintained training recipe is in recipes/gpn_training. Note that the existing benchmark source (Tang et al. 2025) did not use gpn-brassicales: it evaluated a custom GPN pre-trained on the human reference genome.

run_guide.summary: Install the gpn package with inference extras, load the published GPN checkpoint, and score SNVs from a table against a reference genome.
prerequisites: For CUDA, install PyTorch with the official PyTorch installer before or alongside GPN. The sources state no GPU type or memory for inference.
Your own inputs: a variants table (for example variants.parquet) of biallelic SNVs with one-based pos, and the matching reference genome FASTA. The published checkpoint is for Brassicales genomes.
Code and weights are MIT licensed. The weights are not gated.

steps.title: Install
steps.explanation: Installs the gpn package with the file-backed inference commands. The PyPI release is not pinned to the commit read here.

quotes.text: pip install "gpn[inference]"

steps.title: Load the published checkpoint
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from gpn import register_auto_classes
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM

register_auto_classes("ss")

model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("songlab/gpn-brassicales")
PY
steps.explanation: The GPN quick-start snippet from the documentation, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the gpn-brassicales weights and loads them as a masked language model.

quotes.text: register_auto_classes("ss")
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("songlab/gpn-brassicales")

steps.title: Score variants
steps.shell:
gpn ss vep \
  --input-path variants.parquet \
  --genome-path genome.fa.gz \
  --window-size 512 \
  --model-path songlab/gpn-brassicales \
  --output-path scores.parquet \
  --per-device-eval-batch-size 64
steps.explanation: The documented variant scoring command. variants.parquet and genome.fa.gz are the user's own files; positions are one-based and the reference allele must match the genome.

quotes.text: --input-path variants.parquet
--model-path songlab/gpn-brassicales
--output-path scores.parquet
--per-device-eval-batch-size 64
The reference allele must match the local genome or MSA at `chrom:pos`; inference stops on a mismatch.

outputs: scores.parquet, with one row per input variant. Its score column is the raw, uncalibrated alternate-minus-reference log-likelihood ratio averaged over both strands; negative values mean the alternate is less likely.
limitations: These commands were read from the documentation and have not been executed by Rewire.
pip installs the latest PyPI release, not the commit read here; the documentation pins Transformers exactly in the package metadata.
Inference defaults to FP32 without compilation; on GPU the documentation suggests adding --bf16-full-eval --torch-compile.

notes: This page covers single-sequence GPN (GPN-SS), whose published checkpoint is songlab/gpn-brassicales. GPN-MSA has its own page (PR 399) and songlab/gpn-animal-promoter is the separate record 18-gpn-promoter in this batch. The existing source (Tang et al. 2025) evaluated a custom GPN pre-trained on the human reference genome (labelled GPN (human) in its tables), not the published Brassicales checkpoint, so its results should not be read as results for gpn-brassicales. The papers are CC BY-NC-ND, so their bytes are not stored.
